xref.title: Chaotic New York Concert (May 15, 1980)
xref.body: Public Image Limited (P.I.L.), led by Johnny Lydon (formerly Johnny Rotten), agreed to play two nights at the Ritz in New York for a $12,000 fee, despite internal squabbles, drug abuse, and money problems. The band was in no shape to play, lacking a drummer (the sixth one quit) and a bass player (who had just walked out). They quickly hired a 65-year-old jazz drummer from a Broadway music shop. Instead of performing live, P.I.L. pantomimed along to their records, hidden from the audience by a large screen with their silhouettes projected by bright white lights. The 1,500 people in the audience were kept waiting in the pouring rain for over an hour, then discovered the band wasn't playing, and Johnny Lydon began taunting and insulting the crowd. This led to a rain of garbage, a storming of the stage, and the destruction of all equipment, with the gig ending after just 25 minutes. "The gig was killed after just 25 minutes."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Post-Graduation Concerts (1991)
xref.body: The band's first concert after their graduation period took place on July 22, 1991, at the Hollywood in Oxford. Despite having played together "off and on for years" and estimated "at least 100 times" before, this gig was described as relatively modest: "five friends, two strobe lights and a smoke machine." A subsequent gig in October at the Jericho Tavern, known for hosting other Oxford bands like Supergrass, Ride, and Slowdive, proved to be a turning point. "The big day that everybody remembers is July 22, 1991. Just when they played a show at the Hollywood in Oxford, their first post-graduation concert."

xref.title: Pasadena Drug Bust (May 15, 1995)
xref.body: At approximately 3:30 AM on Monday, May 15, 1995, in Pasadena, California, Scott Wyland was apprehended by police after being seen leaving the rear of a CD motel with his lights off. Officers, suspecting a drug transaction, found a chunk of Mexican black tar heroin in his wallet upon apprehension. "When they caught up with Scott, the cops found a chunk of Mexican black tar heroin in Wyland's wallet."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Jail Routine (Late 1999)
xref.body: During his time in jail, Wyland lived in a dormitory, waking at 5:30 AM daily. He attended meetings and drug counseling sessions at 7 AM and 7 PM, had a few hours of free time after supper, and lights were out at 10 PM. He was not permitted to listen to music. "He was not allowed to listen to music."

xref.title: Learjet Crash Survival (2008)
xref.body: On September 19, 2008, Travis Barker survived a Learjet 60 crash in Columbia, South Carolina, after performing with one of his side projects. His wife, who was supposed to join him, had a "freaky feeling" and stayed behind. The plane failed to lift off, hit runway lights, crashed through a fence, crossed a highway, and ended against an embankment, killing four of the six people onboard, including the two pilots. Travis and DJ AM survived with severe burns. "Something went very wrong on takeoff. Even though the weather was fine, the plane failed to lift off by the time it reached the end of the runway."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Learjet Crash Survival and Recovery (2008)
xref.body: On September 19, 2008, after a performance in Columbia, South Carolina, Travis Barker boarded a Learjet 60 bound for Van Nuys, California. His wife, sensing a premonition, stayed behind. During takeoff, the plane failed to lift off, hitting runway lights, crashing through a fence, crossing a highway, and ultimately striking an embankment. Four of the six occupants, including both pilots, died. Travis and DJ AM survived but sustained severe burns. The crash was attributed to badly underinflated tires bursting, leading the pilot to abort takeoff at an unsafe speed. Travis endured 16 surgeries over nearly three months, faced potential foot amputation, and suffered severe PTSD. "It was touching go for Travis for a very long time. He was in and out of hospitals and burn units for nearly three months."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Travis Barker's Plane Crash (2008)
xref.body: On September 19, 2008, less than a month after Jerry Finn's death, Travis Barker and DJ AM were involved in a Learjet 60 plane crash in Columbia, South Carolina, after a show. The chartered plane, which Travis was persuaded to take by DJ AM, suffered underinflated tires that burst during takeoff, causing the landing gear to collapse and the plane to crash through lights, a fence, across a highway, and into an embankment. Travis and DJ AM were the only two survivors from the six people on board. "Then came the plane crash. This was September 19th, 2008."

xref.title: "Dave of Thrones" Tour (2015)
xref.body: After Dave Grohl's severe leg injury in Gothenburg, Sweden, the Foo Fighters returned to touring later that summer with Grohl performing from a specially constructed "Dave of Thrones." This elaborate, over-the-top throne was made of guitar necks and equipped with lights, allowing Grohl to continue playing while recovering from surgery. "The food fighters did return to the stage later that summer with Dave sitting in his Dave of Thrones, a special over-the-top throne made of guitar necks and equipped with lights."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Prolific Collaborator and Producer (2015-2022)
xref.body: Over a seven-year period, Travis Barker became a highly active collaborator and producer, appearing on numerous records. His extensive list of collaborations includes artists such as Young Blood, The Game, M&M, Stevie O'Kee, LL Cool J, Pitbull, Lights, Kenny Hoopla, Machine Gun Kelly, Halsey, Willow Smith, and Dirty Heads. "Travis Barker seemed willing to collaborate and produce just about anyone, and he would appear in a ton of records over the next seven years."

xref.title: Death (May 17–18, 2017) – MGM Grand Detroit, Ativan, Unknown Barbiturates, Naloxone Found in System
xref.body: After a Soundgarden show at the MGM Grand in Detroit, Cornell returned to room 1136. His wife Vicki, 2,000 miles away in Los Angeles, noticed the house lights flickering via a remote app on Chris's phone and called him at 11:35pm — twenty minutes after he left the stage. His bodyguard Martin had given him two Ativan (lorazepam) tablets beforehand to help him sleep. Cornell told Vicki he was fine but sounded groggy and slurred. Martin was sent to check on him at 12:15am, found the room locked, kicked the door in, found the bathroom locked, kicked that door in, and found Chris on the floor with blood from his mouth and an exercise band around his neck. A hotel medic arrived at 12:56am; paramedics followed; Chris was pronounced dead at 1:30am. The official cause was suicide by hanging. Toxicology found Ativan, unknown barbiturates, and unexplained Nalozone (naloxone, an anti-opioid) in his system. A hidden injury was mentioned in two clinical reports but not in the autopsy. In 2018 Vicki sued Dr. Robert Coblin of Beverly Hills, who had prescribed the Ativan, alleging dangerous over-prescription to a known former addict; the lawsuit settled out of court in May 2021. "Many of us who know Chris well noticed that he wasn't himself during his final hours and that something was very off."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Fyre Festival Withdrawal (2017)
xref.body: Just hours before the disastrous Fyre Festival was scheduled to begin on April 28, 2017, Blink-182 announced via Twitter that they were pulling out. The band cited concerns about their ability to deliver a quality performance, implying doubts about payment and the adequacy of production needs for staging, sound, and lights at the festival. "Regrettably, and after much careful and difficult consideration, we want to let you know that we won't be performing at Fire Fest in the Bahamas."

xref.title: "Dave of Thrones" Performance
xref.body: Following a severe leg break in June 2015, Dave Grohl continued touring with the Foo Fighters by performing from a unique custom-built "Dave of Thrones." This specialized chair, constructed from guitar necks and adorned with lights, enabled him to play while his leg was immobilized during recovery. "The food fighters did return to the stage later that summer with Dave sitting in his Dave of Thrones, a special over-the-top throne made of guitar necks and equipped with lights."

xref.title: "Every Junkie Has a Setting Sun" Quote
xref.body: Ash Boo Shultz quoted Neil Young's phrase "as every junkie has a setting sun" when describing the end of his eight-month drug bender in 2013, which severely impacted the completion of USS's "Advanced Basics" album. "Of course as every junkie has a setting sun, thank you Neil Young. The party ended in November, December and I was lights out for a while."

xref.title: Entry into Recording at Grant Avenue Studios
xref.body: Botrell's career began when his girlfriend's uncle, Bob Lannwaw, owner of Grant Avenue Studios, offered him a chance to hang out after he expressed interest in a job. Botrell learned about recording at night, assisting on sessions, cleaning, and making tea for nine months before securing an assistant position in 1983 or 1984. "I walked in the door of that studio and I looked to the left and there was that MCI console and all those lights. And music was going on in the other room and I was like, man, I want something to do with this."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Epilepsy Diagnosis
xref.body: After collapsing at a gig as a teenager from strobe lights and learning about epilepsy through his civil service job in 1977, Ian experienced his first confirmed epileptic seizure on December 27, 1978, in the band's van returning from their first London gig. He was hospitalized, and after being on a waiting list, saw a specialist on January 23, 1978 (transcribed year, likely 1979 in context), who prescribed anti-convulsive drugs. "This was Ian's first confirmed epileptic seizure."

xref.title: Extensive Media Contributions
xref.body: The band has contributed music to numerous media projects, including the 2004 film *Friday Night Lights*, various BBC programs, documentaries, TV shows like *CSI*, and video games such as *Street Fighter* and *Major League Baseball 2K12*. "You may know them from the music from the 2004 film Friday Night Lights, along with a bunch of other movies. They've also contributed music to some BBC programs, a series of documentaries, TV shows like CSI, and video games such as Street Fighter, and Major League Baseball 2K12."

xref.title: First Wave Ska Originator
xref.body: Desmond Dekker was an originator of the "first wave" of Ska, a style born in Jamaica in the 1950s. Along with Toots and the Maytals and The Skatalites, these artists comprised the initial pioneers of the genre. "Those originators, Desmond Decker, Tutson the Maytaws, the Scott lights and so on, all from Jamaica comprised that first wave."

xref.title: Key Figure in New York Indie Rock Revival
xref.body: LCD Sound System became a prominent band in the New York indie rock revival, a scene that also featured groups such as The Strokes, Yeah Yeah Yeahs, and Interpol. "LCD Sound System was one of the leading lights of the New York indie rock revival that also included bands like The Strokes and The Ye-Ye-As and Interpol."

xref.title: Marilyn Manson's Planned Fragrance and Cosmetics Line
xref.body: Marilyn Manson has expressed intentions to launch his own fragrance, possibly a perfume or toilet water, and subsequently a line of cosmetics. His interest in cosmetics is underscored by his status as one of MAC Cosmetics' best customers, a brand favored by performers like Manson and Robert Smith of The Cure for its durability under hot stage lights. "Manson wants to launch his own fragrance, a perfume or a toyler water or something."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: On-Stage Seizures and Collapse
xref.body: Ian Curtis's epilepsy frequently affected his live performances. During one studio session, he fell, hit his head on a sink, and lay unconscious. Strobe lights at a show once induced a seizure, requiring him to be carried off stage, an event that was not isolated, as he collapsed regularly during gigs. "One night in the studio, he fell and hit his head on the sink and laid unconscious on the floor. During a show that featured strobe lights, a seizure was induced and he had to be carried off stage. And that wasn't the first time. Ian collapsed during gigs almost regularly."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Origin of Glasses
xref.body: Costello began wearing his signature glasses due to severe headaches, which he believed were probably brought on by the bright fluorescent lights in the computer room where he worked for Elizabeth Arden. This practical necessity became a defining part of his visual identity. "He also developed severe headaches, probably brought on by the bright fluorescent lights in the computer room. That's when he started wearing those glasses."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: What's The Big Deal About Elvis Costello

xref.title: Performance-Related Seizures
xref.body: Ian Curtis experienced grand mal seizures during at least two performances, one triggered by strobe lights and another so violent that audience members feared for his life. His condition deteriorated to the point where even percussion effects could induce an epileptic episode, leading to a minder being assigned to ensure he took his medication, avoided alcohol, and got sufficient sleep. "There were at least two occasions when he had a grand mal seizure in the middle of a performance. One triggered by strobe lights and another that was so violent, people were genuinely afraid that he was going to die."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Post-Kurt Cobain Legacy
xref.body: After Kurt Cobain's death, fans wondered what material he had left behind. The *With the Lights Out* box set, released over 10 years later, addressed this by compiling remaining material, but it was noted that "the real answer was not much" in terms of truly finished works. "And Kurt died, fans wondered what he had left behind. Had to be something, right? Well, the real answer was not much."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Psychedelic Light Show Technique
xref.body: Pink Floyd's famous psychedelic light shows of the 1960s were produced using a unique and simple method. The band created their distinctive visual effects by stretching condoms over the lenses of their lights and then splattering them with paint and oil. "Their famous psychedelic light show back in the 1960s was created by stretching a condom over the lens of the lights and then spattering it with paint and oil."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Radium Drumstick Solo
xref.body: Viola Smith was known for her flamboyant and physical performances, including drum solos using drumsticks dipped in radium. This created a visually striking effect where, in darkness, only the "dismembered drumsticks flying around" would be visible to the audience, making her a memorable performer. "sometimes performed solos using drum sticks that had been dipped in radium. So the lights would go out and then all the audience would see where these dismembered drumsticks flying around."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Robert Smith's Preference for MAC Cosmetics
xref.body: Robert Smith of The Cure is noted as a loyal customer of MAC Cosmetics, a brand favored by performers like Marilyn Manson. This preference is attributed to MAC products' ability to hold up well under the hot lights of a stage. "A lot of performers like Manson and Robert Smith are the cure for Mac because it holds up nicely under hot stage lights."

xref.title: Touring Practice – Local Backing Band Requirements
xref.body: For his performances, Chuck Berry required the local backup band to be familiar with all his songs and to consist of a drummer, a pianist, and one bass player. They needed to be available for at least three hours prior to showtime for rehearsal, even though Chuck himself often showed up only five minutes before the lights went down. "The local band had to be familiar with all of Chuck's songs, and must include a drummer, a pianist, and one bass player."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: U2's Mentorship on Tour
xref.body: While on tour with U2, Kings of Leon received invaluable guidance on the intricacies of the "business side of touring," including lessons on lighting and creating a distinctive stage show. Jared Followill noted U2's meticulous attention to detail, such as washing lights before every performance. This contrasted sharply with Kings of Leon's own practice of often foregoing soundchecks, with their first chord of a show often being their initial chord of the evening. "They kind of took us under their wings for that whole tour and taught us a lot of stuff that we still use to this day. On the business side of touring stuff. As far as lighting and just having a really big, unique show."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Wife's Concern and Remote Light Flickering
xref.body: After his performance, Chris Cornell returned to room 1136 at the MGM Grand Hotel with his bodyguard, Martin Kirsten. Meanwhile, his wife, Vicki, in Los Angeles, noticed the lights in their home flickering on and off, controlled remotely by an app Cornell used. This unusual activity prompted her to call him at 11:35 PM, about 20 minutes after he left the stage. "Meanwhile, out in Los Angeles, Chris's wife, Vicki, noticed that the lights in the house were flicking on and off. Chris had an app that let him control the lights remotely."
